item.title: US scraps greenhouse gas rules for power plants
item.description:
The EPA announced it is repealing rules limiting greenhouse gas emissions from coal and gas-fired power plants. The move eliminates requirements that would have forced some power plants to sharply reduce their emissions, including through technologies such as carbon capture and storage. Geoff Bennett discussed what this rollback means with Vickie Patton of the Environmental Defense Fund.

item.title: Nato jets down drone that entered Lithuanian airspace
item.description:
The drone, which reportedly entered from Belarus, ⁠was shot down near Pratkunai village in central-southern Lithuania Nato fighter jets shot down a drone over Lithuania after an alert was issued in the ‌capital, Vilnius, and surrounding region, while Poland scrambled fighter jets less than a day after retrieving a suspected Russian drone adrift in its waters. The Lithuania drone ⁠was shot down near the central-southern village of Pratkunai outside the city of Kaunas, said emergency authorities early on Tuesday. The drone came from neighbouring Belarus and was heading west, according to information from Lithuania’s crisis management centre that was reported by national radio LRT. Continue reading...

item.title: US confirms it has weapons in space
item.description:
The US Space Force on Monday confirmed for the first time that Washington has weapons deployed in orbit, as the United States, China and Russia expand their military capabilities in space. The disclosure highlights a growing focus on controlling the space domain and protecting satellites vital to military communications, surveillance and navigation.

item.title: Houthis seize strategic Red Sea islands as analysts warn of impending oil crunch
item.description:
The militant group in Yemen captured the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish, near the chokepoint of the Bab al-Mandab strait Yemen’s Houthi militants have seized two strategic islands in the Red Sea, reinforcing the Iran-backed group’s ability to control a key shipping route, as concerns mount that the world is facing a new oil supply crisis. The seizure of the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish is the latest in the militant group’s swift advance across Yemen’s Red Sea coast, after the capture of the port of Mokha and Perim island in the Bab al-Mandab strait. item.title: Iran war live: 54 Saudi air strikes target Houthis as Yemen fighting rages
item.description:
On Sunday, President Donald Trump reacted to a Wall Street Journal report that highlighted Chinese entities’ role in strikes that killed three American service members and wounded four others in Jordan. The president said that “we spy on them” and China “spies on us.” According to the report, Iran received high-resolution satellite images of the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before striking the base. Iran then launched a ballistic missile attack on the base on July 17, striking a housing area where troops were sleeping. U.S. officials have not accused the Chinese government of direct involvement. When senior U.S. officials shared imagery concerns with their Chinese counterparts, the Chinese officials demanded proof. item.title: A New DHS Report Proves Alligator Alcatraz Detainees Were Right All Along
item.description:
Alligator Alcatraz, the notorious immigrant detention camp erected in the Florida Everglades last year, routinely held detainees in “small metal enclosures” with just 18 square feet of floor space, a practice that the Department of Homeland Security’s independent watchdog called “highly unconventional and does not align with standards for humane treatment,” according to a DHS Office of Inspector General report . First revealed by The New York Times on Monday morning, the document provides a rare comprehensive glimpse of life inside the facility, erected by Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis’s administration last year. Consisting of several soft-sided tents on a remote airfield surrounded by swampland, Alligator Alcatraz at its peak housed up to 1,500 immigrant detainees when DHS was short on detention beds in other facilities. item.title: Sweden’s far right is down, but not yet out. Left and centre leaders must seize this opportunity | Cas Mudde
item.description:
The danger is that other parties just channel the far right – and that will make them vulnerable. Better to fully commit to a progressive agenda After the previous Swedish general election, in 2022, the leaders of the two biggest Swedish parties made a risky decision. Jimmie Åkesson , the leader of the far-right Sweden Democrats (SD), chose to support the rightwing minority government of the Moderate party prime minister Ulf Kristersson , while Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrats’ leader, decided to copy the “Danish model” in an attempt to regain power. In both cases, the strategy led to electoral loss but political success .
